Anya L: Quick heads-up — perf run on staging vs private: prefix cache hit-rate is WAY lower on Private nodes (~62%) vs Hosted (~80%) and Dedicated (~78%). Root cause still fuzzy, attaching quick notes.
Samir K: Numbers? and which models/seq len? :thinking:
Anya L: Model: rw-13b-qlora, typical seq 512. Run: 10k requests sampled. Breakdown:
- Hosted: 80.3% hit
- Dedicated: 77.9% hit
- Private (VPC, on-prem NFS): 62.1% hit
Latency p50 delta ~ +22ms on private for first-token.
Jia P: Oof. Any differences in cache keying or normalization between deploys?
Anya L: That's my suspicion. We profiled the keyer and noticed in Private the client-ip tag is being appended for VPC-origin requests due to a legacy config. That fragments keys.
Samir K: Can you paste the keying snippet?
Anya L: sure — simplified version we traced: ```python
def make_cache_key(prompt, user_ctx):
    prefix = normalize(prompt)
    # legacy: include source for auditing in private installs
    origin_tag = user_ctx.get('source_tag') or ''
    return f"{prefix}::orig={origin_tag}"
```
Anya L: In Hosted/Dedicated source_tag is empty. In Private it comes from the edge (client-ip hashed) for audit reasons -> massive key entropy.
infra-bot: perf-ci/2026-01-17: kv-cache-key-variation test finished — flagged config difference: `cache.include_origin=true` on private clusters
Ops Rep: We enabled that flag for compliance last quarter, didn't realize it impacts prefix cache. Ops can relax it to `include_origin_for_audit_only=true` and route audits to separate logger.
Jia P: Also check storage layer. Private nodes use NFS mount with 7-12ms ops vs Hosted SSD-backed local cache <1ms. Even with misses, higher I/O increases perceived penalty and reduces effective hit warmup.
Samir K: Good point — I/O amplifies cold penalties. Any batching/kernel selection differences?
Anya L: Yes — interestingly kernel selector chose the FP16-kernel path on Hosted which supports bulk KV prefetch (fewer lookups per step). Private falls back to a compatibility kernel that does per-token lookups. Combined with fragmented keys -> explosion of small reads.
Samir K: So two orthogonal issues: key fragmentation (config) + kernel fallback + slower storage. Multiply and you lose hit-rate & latency.
Jia P: Actionable: 1) disable origin tag for cache keying in Private rollout (or hash to coarse bucket) 2) add warmup script to prepopulate common prefixes (script below) 3) plan kernel backport or tweak selector to prefer bulk-prefetch path when seq distribution matches.
Anya L: Warmup script I prototyped (bash): ```bash
# simple warmup: replay top-50 prompts
for p in $(cat top_prompts.txt); do
  curl -s -X POST $RENDER_API -d @- <<EOF
{"prompt": "$p", "model": "rw-13b-qlora"}
EOF
done
```
Samir K: For kernel selector: maybe add config override flag on Private to allow the optimized kernel when GPU driver >= X and qkv-layout matches. I'll open a patch.
infra-bot: perf-alert: scheduled canary next week on private-nonprod with keying change toggled.
Ops Rep: I'll schedule config change in staging then nonprod canary. Need a rollback plan.
Jia P: Also add a quick telemetry check — report `cache_hit_rate`, `avg_kv_latency_ms`, `kernel_variant` per host. Canary should compare those.
Anya L: Agreed. I added a short perf dashboard query for those metrics.
Samir K: Cool. If anyone sees a regression after toggling, ping me. Otherwise we'll roll to prod. :thumbsup:
Anya L: Thanks all — plan is: toggle keying, run warmup, canary kernel override, collect metrics. I'll post results in this thread.
Ops Rep: ack, I'll coordinate change window.
Jia P: +1 — add notes to release doc about compliance implications so security knows why we removed origin from keying.
Anya L: noted. Will include an audit log export path so compliance still gets data without fragmenting cache. :white_check_mark:
